name: Escitalopram Oxalate
sections: Fine white to slightly yellow powder (oxalate), sparingly soluble in water.

The therapeutically active S-enantiomer of citalopram; approved for major depression in 2002 and generalised anxiety disorder in 2003. First approval/introduction: US FDA August 2002 (Lundbeck / Forest Laboratories).

S-enantiomer of citalopram; the most selective SSRI. Inhibits serotonin reuptake at the presynaptic transporter, with allosteric binding that prolongs transporter blockade. Receptor / target profile: The most SERT-selective SSRI, binding both orthosteric and allosteric sites (Ki 0.8–1.1 nM); negligible NET/DAT activity.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80%; Tmax ~4 h. ~56% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life ~27–32 h.

Dizziness, tremor, agitation, somnolence, seizures, QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care with ECG monitoring.
